subject: Condition-name
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.4.3 'Condition-name-1 shall be associated with a switch-name in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.' OK, SR1). The only names SwitchCondOf admits as Format 1 are those registered in SwitchConditions, which is populated solely by BindImplementorNameEntry from a SPECIAL-NAMES switch-name entry whose implementor row is a Switch (a non-switch row with ON/OFF STATUS is COBOL2241, an unknown name registers nothing), plus InheritConfiguration from a containing program's SPECIAL-NAMES. A bare word that is neither a level-88 nor so associated is not a condition (probe n3: the switch's mnemonic-name SW1 used as a condition -> COBOL2318 naming §8.8.4.6). Positive runtime evidence in p1.cob at 85 and 2023 (see FMT-8.4.4.2). Resolution order level-88 before switch (NC211A) only matters for a name that is both, which is already non-conforming source under §8.3.2.2 uniqueness — not this rule's question. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#BindImplementorNameEntry (kb/Work PB2355 extracted the SPECIAL-NAMES binding out of DataBinder.Switches.cs into the SpecialNamesBinder class (its partial files) and the configuration-section services DataBinder keeps into DataBinder.Configuration.cs; each member is the same rule, moved with its body unchanged) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#SwitchConditions (kb/Work PB2355 extracted the SPECIAL-NAMES binding out of DataBinder.Switches.cs into the SpecialNamesBinder class (its partial files) and the configuration-section services DataBinder keeps into DataBinder.Configuration.cs; each member is the same rule, moved with its body unchanged)
